title: Cokernel presentation of the supported constant pro-etale coefficient sheaf
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $j:U=X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. On the small pro-etale sites with their small skeleta [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $A_T$ be the constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and use ordinary sheaves of $A_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $j_!$ be extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero] and $i_*$ the underived module direct image [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image]. Let $\epsilon:j_!A_U\to A_X$ be the open adjunction counit, using $j^{-1}A_X=A_U$, and let $\rho:A_X\to i_*A_Z$ be the constant restriction map, whose component on a weakly etale $W\to X$ sends a constant section $a$ to the same constant on $W\times_X Z$. Then
$$j_!A_U\xrightarrow{\epsilon}A_X\xrightarrow{\rho}i_*A_Z\longrightarrow0$$
is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Equivalently $\rho$ is a cokernel of $\epsilon$ in the abelian category of ordinary module sheaves. No quasi-compactness assumption on $j$ or finiteness assumption on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Section 9, proof of Theorem 9.4 on p. 67; Stacks Tag 095L (etale-cohomology, lemma-ses-associated-to-open) is the etale model only. Pro-etale constant-coefficient extension without quasi-compactness is agent-formulated by local lifting of locally constant functions.

proof.text: Construct the fixed-scalar module sheaf of continuous functions to the discrete ring ULift A. The continuous-function sheaf theorem for the fpqc topology restricts to the pro-etale site. The constant-function map is locally surjective on its open fibres; it is locally injective on nonempty objects, and the empty cover treats the empty object. Local bijectivity and sheafification identify the constant module with this sheaf. Uniqueness of sheafification identifies the specified closed constant restriction with precomposition by the pullback projection.

source.place: Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 4.2.12; Mathlib continuousMapPresheaf and locally bijective sheafification criteria.

proof.text: The open restriction of a closed direct image is zero because the two ranges are disjoint. Under the open extension/restriction adjunction the fixed-scalar counit followed by closed restriction is therefore zero. Transport through the intrinsic coefficient equivalence and the normalized rank-one comparisons gives epsilon followed by rho equals zero.

source.place: Milne Section 9, proof of Theorem 9.4; the complementary-range vanishing theorem in LowerShriek.Open.Complement.

proof.text: For a section on the closed pullback, every point in that closed subspace has an ambient open neighbourhood on which the section is constant: extend its open fibre by the subspace topology. Outside the closed image use its open complement and zero. These neighbourhoods cover the ambient object and are a Zariski, hence pro-etale, cover. Thus restriction of functions is locally surjective. The comparison from Step 1 and coefficient realization transport this to epimorphic rho. This works directly on arbitrary site objects without an affine or finite subcover argument.

source.place: Milne Section 9, proof of Theorem 9.4; agent-written ambient-open version of the finite-cover argument.

proof.text: The fixed-scalar constant open map is the continuous sheafification comparison and is an isomorphism. Its adjoint counit is monic by the existing open-extension monicity criterion and becomes invertible on restriction to the open. A section of the kernel of closed restriction, expressed as a continuous function by Step 1, vanishes on the closed pullback. Cover the ambient object by its open fibres. On a zero fibre lift by zero. A nonzero fibre has no point over the closed subscheme: otherwise surjectivity of the scheme pullback onto pairs of matching points contradicts vanishing. It therefore factors through the complementary open, where the counit is invertible, and the section lifts. The counit-to-kernel factor is thus locally surjective and monic, hence an isomorphism. Transport the resulting limit kernel fork through intrinsic coefficient realization and the source, middle and target comparison isomorphisms.

source.place: Milne Section 9 and the clopen-fibre kernel calculation of Stacks Tag 09AH; open-extension monicity and localization are already proved in the source library.

proof.text: An epimorphism in an abelian category is the cokernel of its kernel. Apply Abelian.epiIsCokernelOfKernel to the kernel fork of Step 4 and the epimorphism of Step 3, with the zero composite of Step 2. This gives exactly the stated IsColimit cofork, with all original definitions and hypotheses unchanged.

split_report.summary: Repair of the returned delivery: added one statement-only finite-constant-section node, citing Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 4.2.12. Proved local surjectivity using a finite affine Zariski cover of each affine object, with affine quasi-compactness and closed base change cited. Constructed an explicit inverse from the kernel to extension by zero using the clopen nonzero locus, then checked both inverse equations by gluing and the module-sheafification universal property. Removed strict henselizations, partition descent, idempotent lifting and any use of the quasi-compact-open localization theorem.

The descendant lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback uses this constant-coefficient source presentation.

lean.statement: theorem proEtale_supported_constant_presentation (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A] {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] : ∃ h : proEtaleOpenConstantCounit i.openComplement.ι A ≫ proEtaleClosedConstantRestriction i A = 0, Nonempty (IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ (proEtaleClosedConstantRestriction i A) h))
